norovirus.note: 2 or more linked cases within 48 hours, residents and staff. Norovirus Working Party, Guidelines for the management of norovirus outbreaks in acute and community health and social care settings (2012, published by PHE on gov.uk): 'two or more cases linked in time and place'; the 48-hour window as in local care-home guidance, e.g. Bolton Council, Diarrhoea & Vomiting (Enteric) Outbreaks in Care Homes flow chart: 'If there is 2 or more linked cases within 48 hours'. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/norovirus-managing-outbreaks-in-acute-and-community-health-and-social-care-settings

flu.note: 2 or more linked resident cases within 5 days; staff cases are managed and logged but don't count. UKHSA, Management of acute respiratory infection outbreaks in care homes (updated 24 July 2024): '2 or more ARI or ILI cases in epidemiologically-linked residents', with 'a 5-day window for case onset'. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/acute-respiratory-disease-managing-outbreaks-in-care-homes/management-of-acute-respiratory-infection-outbreaks-in-care-homes-guidance

norovirus.note: 48 hours after the last case is symptom-free, and at least 72 hours after the last onset. Norovirus Working Party (2012): '48h after the resolution of vomiting and/or diarrhoea in the last known case and at least 72h after the initial onset of the last new case'.

flu.note: 5 days after the onset of symptoms in the most recent resident case. UKHSA (updated 24 July 2024): 'Outbreak measures can be lifted 5 days after the onset of symptoms in the most recent symptomatic resident'.

health.admissions_note: Emergency admissions of care home residents aged 65+ in England: 0.70 per resident per year (0.77 residential, 0.63 nursing), 2016/17. Health Foundation Improvement Analytics Unit, Emergency admissions to hospital from care homes: how often and what for? (2019). https://reader.health.org.uk/emergency-admissions-to-hospital-from-care-homes. Serious falls give their own share (falls.per_resident_year x serious_share); illness gives the rest.

illness.kinds_note: Shares of illness-driven admissions among the three kinds modelled, from the same Health Foundation briefing: pneumonia 12 to 15% and other lower respiratory infections, urinary tract infections 8%, and a smaller share for dehydration; other causes are folded into these three.
illness.illness_note: Severe share, mild illness length and the GP delay are modelling assumptions, not sourced.

health.stay_note: Serious fall or fracture: mean acute stay after hip fracture 16.0 days in England in 2023 (National Hip Fracture Database, via the BGS service review); median 20 days (IQR 11 to 40) in hospital in the year after (REDUCE, Lancet Healthy Longevity 2023). Chest infection: median 5 days for community-acquired pneumonia (BTS national audit 2009/10, mean age 71); care home residents' emergency stays average 8.2 days, 8.9 from residential homes (Health Foundation 2019). UTI: mean 6.4 days in 2023-24 (UKHSA, Understanding the burden of UTI hospitalisations in England, via Care England's briefing). Dehydration: mean 4.6 days for people averaging 80 (ILC-UK, Hydration and older people in the UK, 2018); median 4 days for older patients still dehydrated at 48 hours (Age and Ageing 2014;43 suppl 1).

after_return.note: Care changes after a stay are modelling assumptions: a lasting loss of mobility after a fracture, a few weeks' weakness after an infection.

end_of_life.note: 26.2% of care home residents died within a year (England and Wales cohort, plan-v2 base rates). Most deaths come through a planned end-of-life decline; the length of the decline and the final days are modelling assumptions. Checks hourly during the decline and every 30 minutes in the last days, as care plans usually step up comfort checks as death nears; a 30-minute check for the whole decline (up to four weeks) was missed at the same busy time most days (docs/10).

visitors.note: Assumptions, not fitted: a regular visitor misses about 5 whole weeks a year (about 3 on holiday, mostly in July, August and at Christmas; about 1 ill, mostly in winter; about 1 for family reasons), never more than 1 - reliability of their weeks. Their other weeks are scaled up (reliability / (1 - share of weeks off)) so they visit as often as before on average. Occasional visitors (reliability under 0.5, e.g. Gary in Spain, Tunde monthly) keep their pattern: their quiet weeks are how they visit, not absences. Month factors are normalised over the year.

festivals.name: Christmas
festivals.note: Kept by the whole wing, faith or none.

festivals.name: Vaisakhi
festivals.note: 14 April (Nanakshahi calendar). Raj's card: 'be home for Vaisakhi'.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.note: Lakshmi Puja day, UK dates (Royal Museums Greenwich, rmg.co.uk/stories/time/when-diwali; diwali.info/diwali-dates). Kamala's card: 'go to the temple for Diwali'.

celebrations.note: On a birthday (from the card's dob) or a festival (from the card's faith) every lead visitor comes with their usual chance plus 0.5 (up to 0.95), companions with at least 0.8, arriving 14:00 to 15:00 and staying 1.5 times as long (at least 2 hours). Tea and cake 15:00 to 16:00 in the Lounge (or in their room for someone who doesn't use it), led by Bev when she's on (Mon to Thu), otherwise served with the carers' afternoon tea. No gathering during an outbreak. Assumptions, not fitted.
